Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

at preposition

at a place

classical

Gell. 11.2.5: vestīrī … in forō honestē mōs erat
Sen. Ep. 47.16: in forō et in cūriā

in (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative

at (a place one is in)

Where English says “at” of a place one is in, Latin says “in”: in forō, at the forum; in lūdō, at school; in balneīs, at the baths.

Other words

  • ad (+ accusative) — at, by (beside a place)

    preposition with the accusative · classical · Plaut. Amph. 1020–1021b: Quis ad forēs est?; Liv. 22.7.11: ad portās … multitūdō stetit

    At the edge of a thing, beside it, not in it: ad forēs, at the door; ad portam, at the gate. Ad forum esse, be at the forum, is Plautus’ (Lewis & Short).

  • domī; Rōmae (locative) — at home; at Rome

    locative, without a preposition · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.5.3: suprēmō tē sōle domī, Torquāte, manēbō

    As for “in”: names of towns and small islands, domus, rūs and humus take the locative (see in).

Examples

  • heus, ecquis hīc est? ecquis hoc aperit ōstium? — Quis ad forēs est? — Ego sum.

    Hey, is anybody here? Will somebody open this door? — Who’s at the door? — It’s me.Plaut. Amph. 1020–1021b

  • ad portās major prope mulierum quam virōrum multitūdō stetit, aut suōrum aliquem aut nūntiōs dē iīs opperiēns

    at the gates stood a crowd of women almost larger than the crowd of men, waiting for one of their own or for news of themLiv. 22.7.11

  • vestīrī … in forō honestē mōs erat, domī quod satis erat

    the custom was to dress decently at the forum, and at home as much as was enoughGell. 11.2.5

  • nōn est … quod amīcum tantum in forō et in cūriā quaerās: sī dīligenter attenderis, et domī inveniēs

    there is no reason to look for a friend only at the forum and in the senate house: if you look carefully, you will find one at home tooSen. Ep. 47.16

  • suprēmō tē sōle domī, Torquāte, manēbō

    I shall wait for you at home at sunset, TorquatusHor. Ep. 1.5.3

See also in, next to, at the house of, house.
